business_scope.primary_industry_name: Search Engine Optimization Data Crawler and Keyword Analytics Tool

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3 (Alberta), Part 3 (Limited Partnerships) - s. 51 (registration by Declaration of Limited Partnership), the provisions preserving limited liability of limited partners, and the non-application of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) to limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Companies, Government of Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Alberta Corporate Registry Form LP-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit applies to Alberta limited partnerships. The LP must have at least one general partner with unlimited liability and at least one limited partner. The capital contribution (cash or property) must be agreed and paid at the time or terms stated in the partnership agreement; funds may be held in any Canadian bank account and no escrow is mandated by the Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Alberta Limited Partnership is hereby constituted and registered under the Partnership Act (Alberta), and that the General Partner execute the Declaration of Limited Partnership for filing with the Corporate Registry, Service Alberta. RESOLVED, that subscriptions and capital contributions from limited partners, as recorded in the subscription schedule, are accepted and acknowledged. RESOLVED, that the Partnership's registered office be established at [Registered Office Address], Alberta, where statutory records and the registered office records shall be maintained. RESOLVED, that [General Partner] act as General Partner, and that [Compliance Officer] be appointed Chief Compliance Officer, authorized to open bank accounts and to execute filings with federal, provincial, and municipal authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta via authorized NUANS service providers (electronically available at alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search on the proposed LP name and obtain the NUANS search report. File an application to reserve the approved name for 90 days. The name must include a legal element designating the entity as a limited partnership (e.g., Limited Partnership, LP, L.P.), and must not be confusingly similar to an existing corporate or limited partnership name on the Alberta register. Confirm no confusing trademark conflict with the SaaS brand.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and translation
Name reservation application (if using a service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, select an alternate name and perform a fresh NUANS search. You may also request written reasons from the Director and re-apply with a distinguishable distinctive element; no statutory appeal board exists at this step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and legal counsel; thereafter Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the private Limited Partnership Agreement governing capital contributions (cash or property), profit-sharing, and the general partner's management authority. Complete the Declaration of Limited Partnership naming the general partner, the limited partners, aggregate contributions, the Alberta registered office, and the registered records address. Execute with the approval of the general partner; electronic execution is recognized under the Electronic Transactions Act (Alberta).
required_dossiers: Consent to act as general partner
Consent of owner to use registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting deficiencies with counsel and obtain rectified signatures; ensure the registered office consent is updated; refile the corrected declaration before the registry raises a formal requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Limited Partnership with Corporate Registry and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration via the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal (or courier to the Corporate Registry, 10155 102nd Street, Edmonton). Pay the CAD 140 registration fee for limited partnerships. Retain the filing receipt. The registrar will examine the declaration for compliance with the Partnership Act and issue a Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Certificate of authority if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registrar's Notice of Defective Filing within the stated grace period (typically 30 days) by filing an amended declaration and any supporting consents; late correction fees may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Limited Partnership and Constitute Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership. Establish the partnership records at the Alberta registered office, including the register of limited partners, capital contribution records, and a copy of the partnership agreement. Confirm the exact legal name and date of registration shown on the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction of the certificate by filing a statement of correction with the Corporate Registry if the legal name, address, or date is inaccurate; supply supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint General Partner Representatives and Registered Agent; Open Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner; chartered Canadian bank (Schedule I bank) with anti-money-laundering onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally appoint the general partner's authorized representative and any compliance officer or agent for service. Open a Canadian business bank account in the exact registered LP name presenting the Certificate of Limited Partnership, the partnership agreement, and the business number. Payment rails (Stripe/Paddle) will require a confirmed Canadian bank account and compliance with KYC.
required_dossiers: Passport or government ID of officer or beneficial owner
Bank account application and KYC form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence for SaaS subscription revenues, supply an updated register of partners and a written explanation of the SEO analytics commercial model; escalate to the banking ombudsman only in the case of incorrect refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Business Number and Tax Program Accounts with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through CRA's Business Registration Online portal using the Certificate of Limited Partnership. Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and activate program accounts: GST/HST (mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), payroll (if hiring), and import/export (not required for SaaS). Note: the LP is a pass-through entity; each partner reports its share; the LP itself files an information return (T5013) with the partnership financial statements.
required_dossiers: BN application data and security questionnaire
Partnership agreement and partner SIN or BN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct BN application errors through CRA's Business Enquiry services; if assessed a late-filing penalty, seek cancellation or waiver under CRA taxpayer relief provisions (Form RC4288).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Municipal Business Licence and Data Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority in the Alberta city of operation (e.g., City of Calgary Licensing, City of Edmonton Business Licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the applicable municipal business licence (e.g., Calgary Business Licence Bylaw 23M2004) naming the LP as the operating entity and listing the principal place of business. Confirm home-based business rules if the analytics team operates remotely. Also verify the PIPEDA compliance program for the collection and use of personal information in SaaS analytics (not a licence but a statutory duty).
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused, request written reasons and appeal to the municipal licensing appeal committee; provide zoning and building compliance certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire, Occupational, and Environmental Clearance for Office Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local fire marshal or building inspection authority (e.g., Calgary Fire Department) and Alberta OHS authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the leased office suite, obtain fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code, a building occupancy or structural load clearance under the Alberta Building Code, and an OHS hazard assessment under the OHS Act, SA 2020, c O-2.2. Arrange waste disposal and recycling contracts (including e-waste) with an approved Alberta waste carrier. Pure software operations require no industrial EIA; document non-applicability in the compliance register.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and suite floor plan
Building occupancy or structural load certification
OHS hazard assessment and first aid supplies verification
Waste management and e-waste recycling contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate fire safety deficiencies identified in the inspection report, request a re-inspection, and obtain occupancy only after the fire marshal issues a clearance; keep records for the landlord and insurer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial or manufacturing licensing board mandate for ISIC 6201 (software publishing and SaaS analytics) in Alberta; administrative reference: Alberta Municipal Affairs, Building and Technical Services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required at the provincial level for pure software analytics operations; optional municipal business licence under the applicable City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licence Bylaw.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) - Environmental Assessment Program
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment screening under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12, because the enterprise is a software analytics SaaS with no physical effluent, discharge, or construction triggering a designated activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable operationally; however, leasehold office premises must maintain heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning and indoor air quality per the Alberta Building Code; no wastewater discharge permit under the Water Act, RSA 2000, c W-3; electronic waste must be disposed of through approved recycling channels under Alberta's Recycling Regulation and waste management bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code and local fire authority inspection; structural load and occupancy clearance under the Alberta Building Code for the leased Class-A office suite; occupational health and safety clearance and hazard assessment under the OHS Act, SA 2020, c O-2.2 and the Alberta OHS Code; civil defence clearance: not applicable for an office-based SaaS establishment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online system, My Business Account, Represent a Client, and the GST/HST program account. Alberta has no provincial sales tax; Alberta corporate and partnership filings are administered through the Alberta Corporate Registry, while federal GST/HST administration is conducted by the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Alberta limited partnership should obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) and, where applicable, a GST/HST program account identified by the RT suffix. The filing sequence is: (1) complete Alberta partnership registration and obtain the provincial registration evidence; (2) obtain a BN through CRA Business Registration Online, CRA-authorized representative channels, or the CRA non-resident registration process; (3) submit entity name, Alberta registered office, partnership agreement details, formation date, business activities, responsible partners, foreign ownership information, fiscal year-end, and authorized-contact information; (4) apply for the GST/HST account using Form RC1 or the applicable CRA online registration workflow; (5) provide identity, authority, and formation documents if requested; and (6) maintain CRA account information and file required GST/HST returns. A foreign partner does not generally need a Canadian individual TIN merely to hold an LP interest, but may require a Canadian tax identification number for Canadian tax filings, withholding, treaty claims, or CRA correspondence. The LP may also require a payroll, import-export, or other CRA program account depending on its activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election for an Alberta limited partnership. A valid Canadian partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income-tax purposes, with partnership income and losses allocated to partners under the Income Tax Act and the partnership agreement, subject to statutory restrictions. Available elections are transaction-specific rather than entity-classification elections, including applicable partnership fiscal-period, rollover, allocation, foreign-affiliate, and treaty-related elections. Classification for foreign tax purposes may differ from Canadian treatment; the partnership should obtain a formal Canadian and relevant foreign-jurisdiction classification analysis. Hybrid-mismatch rules, foreign affiliate rules, non-resident withholding provisions, and treaty limitation provisions may apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces. Alberta applies the federal GST and does not impose a provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies, measured under the small-supplier rules. The threshold is generally tested over a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration may be required earlier where the LP ceases to qualify as a small supplier or voluntarily registers. Non-resident digital-economy suppliers may be subject to specialized GST/HST registration rules, depending on the customer base, supply characterization, and applicable platform or simplified-registration regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general federal real-time electronic-invoice clearance or continuous transaction-control mandate for ordinary B2B SaaS supplies. Electronic invoices and records are permitted if they preserve reliability, readability, accessibility, and auditability. GST/HST invoices must contain information required by the CRA, including supplier identity and BN/GST-HST account details where applicable, date, description, consideration, tax rate or amount, and customer information where required for input tax credit documentation. There is no general federal digital tax stamp or pre-approval requirement. Alberta has no provincial sales-tax invoicing regime. Specialized public-sector procurement or contractual e-invoicing requirements may apply separately.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods may generally be zero-rated when exported from Canada and the supplier retains satisfactory evidence that the goods were exported in accordance with the Export and Imported Goods and Services provisions. Services supplied to a non-resident may qualify for zero-rating where the statutory conditions are satisfied, but exclusions apply, including certain services connected with Canadian real property, tangible personal property, litigation, personal services, and services performed in Canada. SaaS, data-crawling, SEO analytics, and electronically supplied services require supply-by-supply analysis, including customer residency, contractual recipient, place-of-supply facts, performance location, use or enjoyment, and whether the service is an excluded Canadian-connected service. A non-resident customer alone does not automatically establish zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, description, value, and destination
Export declaration or applicable Canadian Border Services Agency export reporting record where legally required
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or other carrier evidence for exported goods
Proof of delivery or receipt outside Canada
Contracts, purchase orders, customer residency records, and billing records
Evidence supporting non-resident status and the applicable zero-rating provision for services
Payment records or bank statements evidencing the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general Canadian statutory requirement
GST/HST return, general-ledger, and tax-invoice records supporting the zero-rated supply and any input tax credit claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general foreign-exchange repatriation requirement or statutory deadline for export proceeds. CRA may reassess GST/HST where zero-rating is unsupported, including assessment of tax that should have been collected, denial or recovery of input tax credits and refunds, applicable arrears interest, and penalties. Gross-negligence penalties may generally equal 50% of the understated net tax or overstated refund or credit, subject to the statutory calculation. False statements, omissions, fabricated export evidence, or obstruction may create additional civil penalties and, in serious cases, criminal exposure. Export records and GST/HST books must be retained for the applicable statutory period, generally six years from the end of the relevant year, subject to CRA extensions and special rules. Refunds may be clawed back with interest where the claim was paid on the basis of ineligible or fraudulent documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank of Canada, responsible for monetary stability, Canadian dollar issuance, the national large-value payment-system oversight, and joint management with the Minister of Finance of the Exchange Fund Account. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange licencing commission or capital-controls bureau. Regulatory responsibility for the cross-border banking and FX compliance of an Alberta limited partnership is distributed among: the Bank of Canada (currency, payment-system and retail-payment-activity supervision), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (prudential regulation of Tier-1 banks under the Bank Act and related statutes), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing surveillance, including CAD 10,000 wire and cash transaction reporting), the Department of Finance Canada (economic sanctions and Exchange Fund Account policy), the Alberta Corporate Registry (registration of the limited partnership under the Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c. P-7), and the Alberta Securities Commission (derivatives dealing and over-the-counter hedging regulatory framework for Alberta financial-market participants). The practical effect for the Alberta LP is that no exchange-control approval is required for inbound or outbound funds; instead, transaction-level compliance is enforced through the banks and FINTRAC, with market-conduct and sanctions screening applied at the point of payment settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted the IMF Article VIII obligations and operates a freely floating, fully convertible currency with no exchange-control settlement approvals. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted: the ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 SEO content-analytics tool generates subscription and licensing revenue that may be received in any currency without Bank of Canada or Finance Canada authorisation, and digital services exported from Canada benefit from GST/HST zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act. Capital-account convertibility is equally open: non-resident limited partners may inject cash or assets into the Alberta LP without any foreign-exchange decree, exchange-rate band, or conversion quota. The relevant frictions are not FX-control but rather: (i) FINTRAC reporting by the receiving bank for any wire transfer, including partner capital subscriptions, of CAD 10,000 or more; (ii) federal income-tax compliance under the Income Tax Act, which treats the LP as fiscally transparent, obliges filing of the T5013 Statement of Partnership Income, and taxes each non-resident partner on its allocated share of Canadian-source business income, with the possibility of treaty relief; (iii) Alberta Partnership Act formalities requiring a registered Alberta office, the General Partner's consent, and the Statement of Limited Partnership to be updated for capital changes; and (iv) Investment Canada Act review, which applies only where a foreign acquisition triggers the high monetary review threshold for a 'Canadian business' and does not ordinarily apply to a passive subscription into a lean software start-up LP. Profit remittance presents no statutory hurdle: there is no repatriation tax, no exit-licence, no black-market exchange mechanism, and no prohibition on distributing cash to non-resident partners, provided the LP maintains accurate capital accounts so that distributions represent after-tax or tax-free capital streams rather than untaxed earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable / zero surrender obligation. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to sell export receipts to the central bank or a designated dealer. Cross-border receipts from the SEO analytics and keyword-research software subscriptions are freely retained in CAD, USD, EUR, or any other convertible currency, and may be payable into the LP's operational or capital escrow accounts at a Tier-1 Canadian bank. The only mandatory compliance obligations are: (a) the banks automatically report to FINTRAC all electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; (b) the LP must retain commercial invoices, transfer records, and customer agreements for at least five years under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act / money-service-business record-keeping standards; and (c) where the bank requests a statistical classification, the LP should confirm the purpose code 'INVS' or 'CASH' and the bank will record the inflow on its Bank of Canada balance-of-payments return as non-resident direct investment in a Canadian partnership. No surrender certificates, no central-bank settlement tickets, and no exchange-control endorsements are required for a Canada-resident limited partnership exporting digital services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulation_notes: The Bank of Canada regulates the payment and clearing environment through the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) and the emerging Real-Time Rail (RTR), while Payments Canada operates the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) used by Tier-1 banks for domestic file-based settlement such as Stripe and Paddle merchant payouts. Banks are also subject to OSFI capital and liquidity rules and to the federal economic sanctions administered under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, which require transactional screening of all cross-border wires, including inbound partner capital subscriptions and outbound SaaS vendor payments. FINTRAC does not require prior approval of a wire transfer but will receive an electronic funds transfer report for any single transfer equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000; the bank may pause a transfer where the underlying commercial purpose or beneficial ownership documentation is unsatisfactorily evidenced.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.readiness_score: High - the Alberta LP treasury can begin cross-border banking immediately, provided the General Partner and passive limited partners complete the Tier-1 bank onboarding package and the LP maintains a clean fund-source trail for each partner contribution.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Alberta limited partnership level (flow-through). Corporate partners are taxed on their allocable share: 15% federal general + 8% Alberta general = 23% combined; qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners on first C$500,000 of active business income: 9% federal + 2% Alberta = 11% combined.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED Investment Tax Credit: 35% refundable on qualified expenditures up to C$3M for CCPC partners; 15% for other corporations. Alberta Research and Development Tax Credit: 10% non-refundable. No Alberta small business deduction at the LP level; the CCPC partner eligibility applies.
